plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like flowers. It thrives in mild, humid climates and is widely cultivated in gardens, with thousands of cultivars varying in form from single to fully double blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, peaking in winter
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; widely cultivated in the southeastern United States, Western Europe, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative, is the plant from which all true tea is made, and Camellia japonica seed oil has been used in Japan for hair care for centuries.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous large shrub or small tree that flowers on bare branches in the depths of winter. Its spidery, ribbon-like petals are strongly fragrant and curl up in freezing temperatures to protect themselves, then unfurl when it warms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midwinter, December to February in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; cultivated in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The petals of witch hazel roll up tightly during frosty nights and expand again when temperatures rise, a natural form of frost protection.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: A clump-forming perennial with strap-like leaves and tall stems topped by rounded clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere it is at the height of its summer bloom in early January.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (December to February in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South Africa; naturalized and cultivated in Australia, New Zealand, and coastal California
plants.funFact: Despite its common name, it is not a true lily; the name Agapanthus comes from Greek words meaning 'love flower'.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with feathery fern-like leaves that becomes covered in clusters of vivid scarlet-orange blooms. It is a showy shade tree in tropical and subtropical regions and flowers in the warm months of the Southern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); also blooms in the tropical dry season elsewhere
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; cultivated across the tropics including northern Australia, Brazil, and southern Africa
plants.funFact: Although abundant in cultivation, the flame tree is considered endangered in its native Madagascar due to habitat loss.
